newsitem.title: USA: U.S. muni groups urge issuers to understand munis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. muni groups urge issuers to understand munis.

text.p: State and local government groups on Tuesday urged municipal officials to have a "thorough understanding" of the tax-exempt bonds they plan to offer to investors.

The recommendation is in the new "Pocket Guidelines for Elected and Other Public Officials" released this week by the Government Finance Officers Assocation (GFOA), National League of Cities, National Association of Counties and National Association of State Auditors, Comptrollers and Treasurers.
The brochure, which had input from the Securities and Exchange Commission, comes in the wake of SEC's enforcement actions concerning Orange County, Calif. and Maricopa County, Ariz. bond offerings.
The SEC said the counties inadequately disclosed key information to investors about that state of their finances.
The brochure urged localities, for instance, to have procedures in place for selecting qualified financial advisors, dealers, and bond lawyers for bond deals.
"How are they being compensated?," the brochure asks about professionals. "How are we relying on them, and is our reliance appropriate?"
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt called the pocket guide a "great step forward. Every elected official should read this booklet before approving a bond issues."
The groups that produced the pocket guide are making copies available to their members and 23 other national organizations representing the muni market.
